scores.claim_text: Redwire performs directly or through prime contractors for U.S. national security agencies including U.S. Army, U.S. Marine Corps, U.S. Air Force, U.S. Space Force, DARPA, and the NRO; and civil agencies including NASA. Federal-government customer base is the dominant revenue source.
scores.interpretation: Strong corroboration. 117 federal contracts totaling $238.6M aggregate value across NASA, DoD/AFRL, and prime-subcontracts — multiple Redwire legal-entity recipient names appear (Redwire Space Inc, Redwire Space Solutions, Redwire Space Technologies, Loadpath — known Redwire subsidiaries). Largest single award is the NASA Tipping Point in-space robotic manufacturing/assembly contract ($87.6M). DoD awards include the Air Force SCARLET truss program ($10.6M) and ELLI ($10.2M). Federal-customer claim is unambiguously supported by Layer-3 USAspending. PASS.

scores.claim_text: Redwire owns proprietary 'patented and award-winning' Roll-Out Solar Array (ROSA) technology and a portfolio of space sensors/avionics/payloads with '50 years of on-orbit heritage', plus a broad spacecraft platform lineup (SabreSat, Phantom, Hammerhead, Thresher, Mako).
scores.M_check: uspto_odp.query_assignee across known Redwire subsidiary names

rosa_specific_patents_at_DSS: 9611056 — DIRECTIONALLY CONTROLLED ELASTICALLY DEPLOYABLE ROLL-OUT SOLAR ARRAY (granted 2017)
10239642 — HINGE AND LOCK MECHANISM FOR ROLL-OUT SOLAR ARRAY
9899559 — MODULAR PHOTOVOLTAIC PANEL ASSEMBLIES FOR SPACE SOLAR ARRAYS

scores.interpretation: ROSA patent ownership concretely supported. Although the 'Redwire' assignee yields only 3 granted patents directly, the technology lineage is verifiable through known acquired subsidiaries: Deployable Space Systems (ROSA inventor — explicit DIRECTIONALLY CONTROLLED ELASTICALLY DEPLOYABLE ROLL-OUT SOLAR ARRAY patent #9611056 granted 2017; HINGE AND LOCK MECHANISM FOR ROLL-OUT SOLAR ARRAY #10239642), Made In Space (25 granted, microgravity/in-space manufacturing), and Roccor (15 granted, deployable composite structures). Aggregate ~51 granted patents across the corporate tree — comfortably exceeds the heuristic-8 PASS threshold of >=10. PASS.

scores.claim_text: Redwire is the prime mission integrator on DARPA's Otter VLEO air-breathing satellite program using its SabreSat platform, and Phantom is being used on ESA's Skimsat VLEO program.
scores.M_check: usaspending DoD contracts + edgar_fts SabreSat asymmetric-mention test
scores.interpretation: Partial corroboration. DoD aggregate ($70.4M, 12 awards) supports the general defense relationship, but the SPECIFIC DARPA Otter prime-integrator contract does not appear in USAspending awards under DARPA-labeled awarding sub-agency or with 'Otter / VLEO / air-breathing' keywords in descriptions. The top DoD awards are AFRL space-structures programs (CALL 002 ASSIST, SCARLET, ELLI), not DARPA Otter. DARPA prime-integrator awards at $-millions normally ARE in USAspending under 'Department of Defense'; absence here is mild evidence of either (a) Otter being a very recent OTA award not yet reflected, or (b) Redwire being a sub on someone else's prime. The asymmetric-mention test on SabreSat is also a soft yellow flag: 16 SEC hits but 0 from external filers — entirely Redwire's own 8-K/10-Q. The ESA Skimsat reference is in a foreign-agency jurisdiction (heuristic 5: ESA off-EDGAR) and is UNVERIFIABLE. Net: claim is partially supported by the broader DoD relationship; the specific Otter prime-integrator label is not yet independently verifiable. MODERATE.

scores.claim_text: Redwire has launched 42 PIL-BOX (Pharmaceutical In-space Laboratory Bio-crystal Optimization eXperiment) payloads through Dec 31, 2025 for partners 'including, but not limited to, Bristol Myers Squibb and Eli Lilly', with eleven active payload facilities built by Redwire on the ISS.
scores.M_check: edgar_fts counterparty disclosure (BMS, Eli Lilly) + PIL-BOX asymmetric mention
scores.interpretation: Counterparty-disclosure test fails: zero mentions of Redwire in BMS or Eli Lilly SEC filings. However, this is a soft signal because pharma microgravity research budgets at BMS/Lilly scale ($40B+ revenue) sit far below SEC-materiality-disclosure thresholds — heuristic 7 says ABSENCE while claiming a named commercial customer is a yellow flag, NOT a hard contradiction at this magnitude. Likewise PIL-BOX appears in 12 SEC filings — all 12 are Redwire's own 8-K/10-Q exhibits. Zero asymmetric/external mentions. The 42-payload count and the 11-active-ISS-payload-facilities counts are physical-launch claims that could be checked against NASA mission manifests, which are off-EDGAR. UNVERIFIED rather than SEVERE because (a) PIL-BOX is a real Redwire product line with substantial NASA ISS contracts visible in USAspending (multiple Redwire JSC task orders for bio-crystal / microgravity), and (b) counterparty disclosure is sub-materiality for BMS/Lilly. UNVERIFIED.

scores.claim_text: Redwire operates from 28 locations totaling approximately 910,000 sqft (23 in North America across 11 states + 5 in Europe). Headquarters in Jacksonville, FL. North American locations include CA (5), CO (4), FL (2), IN (2), NM (2), MI (2), VA (2), AL, MA, OR and Ontario (1 each).
scores.M_check: epa_frs.query_facilities (Redwire + acquired-subsidiary names) across all claimed US states

M_value.IN_facility: REDWIRE SPACE - GEORGETOWN, 401 EXPLORATION WY, FLOYD COUNTY

scores.interpretation: 1 'Redwire' direct + 3 Adcole (Massachusetts) facilities verified in EPA FRS. Bulk of the claimed footprint (CA, CO, FL HQ, etc.) is not in EPA FRS. Heuristic 1 warns absence is real signal FOR propulsion test sites and launch facilities — but Redwire is overwhelmingly a payload/structures/integration company with clean-room operations, not propellant-handling, so most of their facilities legitimately would not trigger EPA FRS registration thresholds. The single Indiana facility (Floyd County / Georgetown) maps cleanly to one of the two claimed Indiana sites. Adcole-MA matches one of the claimed MA facilities. Footprint claim is plausibly supported; absence of FRS records for the rest is not a hard contradiction at heuristic-1 strength. PASS (with note: physical-footprint magnitude only loosely verified).

scores.claim_text: Defense Tech segment includes Stalker UAS and Penguin UAS. On July 14, 2025, Stalker UAS was granted Authority to Operate by the DIU and placed on the DIU Blue UAS List. Stalker has 'thousands of flight hours across six continents' with U.S. Marine Corps and U.S. Army customers; Penguin C used by Ukraine Armed Forces, Latvia and Lithuania MoD, Royal Saudi Air Force.
scores.M_check: usaspending Edge Autonomy + UAV Factory contracts

M_value.Edge_Autonomy_top_award: N0001925P1000 - VXE30 STALKER UAS purchase order ($1.48M)

scores.interpretation: Mixed corroboration. The acquired Edge Autonomy entity shows just $1.6M of USAspending contracts post-2020 (a single VXE30 STALKER purchase order with the Department of the Navy), plus $61K to legacy UAV Factory (Penguin's original OEM). Foreign sales (Ukraine, Latvia, Lithuania, Saudi) are heuristic-5 off-EDGAR / unverifiable. Stalker's historical USMC/Army deployment heritage predates Edge Autonomy and was largely under Lockheed Martin Skunk Works — making direct USAspending validation difficult under the current entity name. The Edge Autonomy acquisition was just completed June 13, 2025, so the small contract footprint may also reflect entity-name lag in USAspending. The headline-customer claim (USMC, Army) is plausible at the heritage-product level but only $1.5M is independently visible. Penguin C foreign-MoD customers are entirely off-domain. MODERATE — direct evidence is materially below the headline.

scores.claim_text: Material weakness in internal controls over financial reporting (KPMG adverse opinion as of Dec 31, 2025). Net loss of $226.6M on $335.4M revenue in 2025. $94.5M cash + $35M revolver capacity; $88.4M JPMorgan term loan + $47.1M convertible preferred. Net EAC adjustments swung from -$17.7M (2024) to -$54.5M (2025). ATM-financed equity issuance of $518.4M in 2025.

key_atm_prospectus_supplements: 2025-11-10 ATM filing-fee exhibit + ATM prospectus supp

scores.interpretation: Severe distress / quality-of-earnings markers per heuristic 10. KPMG issued an adverse opinion on internal control over financial reporting as of Dec 31, 2025. Two distinct material weaknesses identified (process-level controls; IT general controls). Net loss expanded to $226.6M (-68% operating margin) on $335.4M revenue. EAC unfavorable adjustments are accelerating year-over-year (-$3.5M -> -$17.7M -> -$54.5M) which is a forensic indicator of contract pricing/estimating problems. The 5% gross margin (vs 15% prior year) is barely positive after $13.6M Edge purchase-accounting inventory adjustment. Cash burn from operations was $177M. The company funded itself almost entirely via dilution — $518.4M of ATM/equity issuance in 2025, with at least four distinct 424B5 prospectus supplements (May 2026 already filing more ATM capacity). Convertible preferred PIK dividends (8,068 + 3,312 shares of preferred-on-preferred) plus a $63.9M repurchase from Bain Capital are mezzanine-equity churn. JPM Term loan refi extending out to 2029 was a Subsequent Event (Feb 2026). Combined: material-weakness + adverse opinion + accelerating EAC + heavy ATM dilution + preferred PIK = SEVERE per heuristic 10. (Going-concern language not present, hence not RED_FLAG.) SEVERE.

scores.claim_text: Redwire's solar/power systems are flight-deployed on NASA's Imaging X-ray Polarimetry Explorer (IXPE), NASA's DART, NASA's Artemis I lunar mission, ISS, and Space Force GPS Satellite program. Redwire delivers 'multiple advanced RF payloads for a constellation of satellites for a national security satellite constellation in LEO' (likely Space Development Agency / NRO Proliferated LEO).
scores.M_check: usaspending USSF/SDA/NRO + edgar_fts LMT/NOC/LHX counterparty disclosure

M_value.NASA_IXPE_DART_visible_in_USAspending: NASA solar/structures contracts visible (IXPE/DART/Artemis ROSA subcontract trails through prime missions)

scores.interpretation: Mixed. The 'national security satellite constellation in LEO' claim is a vague / unnamed-program reference (likely SDA or NRO Proliferated LEO) and is NOT verifiable in USAspending top-50 awards under either USSF, SDA, or NRO as awarding agency. None of the three defense primes plausibly involved (LMT, NOC, L3Harris) mention Redwire in their SEC filings — heuristic-7 yellow flag, although Redwire's likely subcontract dollars sit below the primes' segment-disclosure materiality thresholds. The NASA missions (IXPE, DART, Artemis I) are supported by Redwire's NASA contract trail (Tipping Point $87M, multiple JSC task orders). The Space Force GPS Satellite program claim flows through Lockheed prime — not directly visible, but consistent with heritage. External all-filer mention count of Redwire is 423 (robust general SEC visibility, presumably analysts + co-investors). Net: NASA-mission claim is well-supported, defense-constellation claim is materially under-corroborated by USAspending. MODERATE.
